newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel seeks to raise $2.6 bln overseas this year.
newsitem.headline: Israel seeks to raise $2.6 bln overseas this year.

text.p: Israel aims to raise as much as $2.6 billion overseas this year, down slightly from $2.8 billion in 1996, Treasury accountant-general Shai Talmon said on Sunday.

He said the government in its next issue of Yankee bonds planned to seek longer maturities than the 10 years in the issue made last year. Talmon said Israel plans a Yankee issue in fourth-quarter 1997 or first-quarter 1998.
He said Israel aimed to raise $1.25 billion in the framework of the U.S. government guarantees programme. Of that, Israel has already raised $750 million in an offering in January.
In addition, Israel plans to borrow $850 million through its Israel Bonds programme, $150 million through a Samurai issue set for June and $150 million from various other sources, Talmon said.
The Yankee and Samurai issues are being conducted by Israel as part of its programme to test the receptiveness of international financial markets to Israeli issues.

The Samurai issue is to be underwritten by Nomura Securities Co. But Talmon said that if Japanese authorities were to suspend Nomura's capital market activities, Israel would ask Daiwa Securities Co to underwrite it.
Nomura is under investigation by Japanese authorities in connection with alleged payments to a client linked to racketeers.

Talmon said Israel had $1.95 billion left of the $10 billion in loan guarantees quota. The guarantees were granted by the United States in 1992 to help fund the absorption of immigrants from the former Soviet Union.
Talmon said the Treasury intended to raise the remaining $1.95 billion in two or three separate offerings.
